findings.title: Concurrent builds of the same key can replace a newer index with a stale one
findings.body: Moving the cache lock to only the assignment removes the only synchronization between the GetIndex cache miss and BuildIndex. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both build independent indexes and whichever finishes last overwrites the cache. A write event can be applied to the first cached index after its snapshot was built but before the second build publishes; the second, stale snapshot then replaces it and that write is no longer searchable. For file-backed indexes, the concurrent bleve.New calls also contend for the same directory and can make one request fail. Use a per-key singleflight/lock and re-check the cache before building or publishing.

findings.title: Startup index build has an unrecoverable write-event gap
findings.body: The search watcher is started only after all initial BuildIndex calls finish. WatchWriteEvents initializes its SQL polling cursor to the latest resource versions at the time it is called, so writes made by another server after an index's ListIterator snapshot but before line 202 are neither in that snapshot nor replayed by the watcher. The build method returns the snapshot resource version specifically needed to catch up, but it is discarded. In HA deployments this leaves indexes permanently stale until another write to each affected object occurs. Start/watch from a cursor established before the snapshot and replay events after the returned build resource version, or otherwise coordinate snapshot and watch registration.
